crossRefs.note: Pilate therefore went out to them, and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”
When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that prosperity…
I answered them that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction before the accused has met…
if anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having children who believe, who are not accused of loose or unruly…
At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, he who is to die shall be put to death. At the mouth of one witness…
One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin that he sins. At the mouth of two…
and the judges shall make diligent inquisition; and behold, if the witness is a false witness, and has testified…
then you shall do to him as he had thought to do to his brother. So you shall remove the evil from among you.
But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be…
It’s also written in your law that the testimony of two people is valid.
This is the third time I am coming to you. “At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.”
A man who disregards Moses’ law dies without compassion on the word of two or three witnesses.

translations.web: Don’t receive an accusation against an elder, except at the word of two or three witnesses.
translations.bsb: Do not entertain an accusation against an elder, except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
translations.kjv: Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.
translations.asv: Against an elder receive not an accusation, except at the mouth of two or three witnesses.
